summary: Deletes or keeps points or primitives using attribute, thin, pattern, group, and bounding methods. The logic can be built from sequential selection blocks and applied to points or primitives.

key_params.name: linestripbehavior
key_params.note: Split or delete affected line strips

key_params.name: cpureadback
key_params.note: Copy point count and topology information back to CPU

key_concepts: Deletes or keeps selected points or primitives with the Operation menu.
Selection logic can come from attribute comparisons, thinning, index patterns, existing groups, or bounding volumes.
Sequential condition blocks combine with boolean operators such as and, or, xor, nand, and nor.
Topology changes cascade: deleting primitives can remove unused points, while deleting points affects vertices and primitives that reference them.
common_gotchas: Deleting points can trim, split, or remove line strips depending on Line Strip Behavior.
When deleting primitives, unused points and vertices can also be removed.
Complex delete predicates are often easier to debug if a Math Mix POP creates a visible mask attribute first.
